raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The pip / uv and from-source instructions in `docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx` do not list several requirements that a fresh Linux machine needs before `sglang serve` works. The CI bootstrap (`scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`) and the Dockerfile already provide all of them, so the gap only shows up outside those environments, one failure at a time.

On a fresh WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 machine with only the NVIDIA driver installed, following the current page hit these in sequence:

| Missing | Symptom |
| --- | --- |
| Rust toolchain (from source) | `RuntimeError: cargo is required to discover the Rust extension modules ...` |
| C compiler | `UserWarning: Triton is not supported on current platform, roll back to CPU.`, then `Failed to find C compiler` during CUDA graph capture |
| Python headers (system Python venv) | `driver.c: fatal error: Python.h: No such file or directory` |
| CUDA Toolkit / `nvcc` | `Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_fused_rope_...` with `/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc: not found` (also with `flashinfer-jit-cache` installed, since SGLang's own JIT kernels need `nvcc`) |

I reproduced each one on `main` by hiding the corresponding tool inside a single process, and confirmed that a setup following the CI script starts the server on the first try.

Related:
- #29279 proposed similar docs for the old `docs_new/` tree and was closed by the stale bot without review. Its `protoc` step is no longer needed: protobuf bindings are checked in since #41726, and no crate in `rust/` has a `build.rs` or a build-time protoc dependency.
- #20076 reports the `nvcc: not found` JIT failure in runtime containers.
- #18644 added `python3-dev` to CI for the same Triton `Python.h` failure.

## Modifications

`docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx` only:

- **pip / uv tab**: list the CUDA Toolkit 13 (`nvcc`), C compiler, and Python header requirements, including the toolkit lookup order from `python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/compile/toolchain.py` (`CUDA_HOME`/`CUDA_PATH`, then `nvcc` on `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`).
- **pip / uv tab**: create the venv with `--python-preference only-managed`, as the CI script does, so uv uses a Python build that ships `Python.h` even when a system Python 3.12 exists.
- **From source tab**: add the rustup step (the toolchain version comes from `rust/rust-toolchain.toml`) and an accordion for `SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none`, noting that Rust-backed features such as the gRPC server build their extension on first use.
- **Troubleshooting**: add entries for `nvcc not found`, the misleading Triton CPU fallback warning, and `cargo is required`, so the error strings are searchable.

The `git clone -b v0.5.21 ...` line that `scripts/release/bump_docs_install_version.py` rewrites is unchanged, and all existing anchors are kept.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A (docs only).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A (docs only).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (N/A, docs only)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (`mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` passes)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -62,7 +62,10 @@ The container shell is ready for `sglang serve`.
 </Tab>
 <Tab title="pip / uv" id="method-1-with-pip-or-uv">
 
-Use Python 3.11 or higher and a compatible CUDA 13 environment.
+Use Python 3.11 or higher and a CUDA 13 environment that includes:
+
+- **CUDA Toolkit 13 with `nvcc`.** SGLang compiles some CUDA kernels at runtime, so a GPU driver alone is not enough. SGLang looks for the toolkit in `CUDA_HOME` (or `CUDA_PATH`), then the directory of `nvcc` on your `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`.
+- **A C compiler and the Python development headers.** Triton compiles a small launcher when it initializes. On Debian or Ubuntu, install `build-essential`. Python builds managed by uv include the headers; if you use the system Python instead, also install its development package, such as `python3.12-dev`.
 
 <Accordion title="CUDA version compatibility">
 
@@ -79,10 +82,10 @@ pip install --upgrade pip
 pip install uv
 ```
 
-Create and activate a virtual environment:
+Create and activate a virtual environment. `--python-preference only-managed` makes uv use its own Python build, which includes the development headers, even when a system Python 3.12 is installed:
 
 ```bash Command
-uv venv --python 3.12
+uv venv --python 3.12 --python-preference only-managed
 source .venv/bin/activate
 ```
 
@@ -112,7 +115,28 @@ For `CUDA_HOME` errors, see [Troubleshooting](#cuda_home).
 </Tab>
 <Tab title="From source" id="method-2-from-source">
 
-Use Python 3.11 or higher in an activated Python environment, with CUDA dependencies appropriate for the version you build.
+Use Python 3.11 or higher in an activated Python environment. The CUDA Toolkit, C compiler, and Python header requirements from the pip / uv tab also apply.
+
+**Install the Rust toolchain**
+
+Installing from source builds SGLang's Rust extensions with Cargo. Install Rust with [rustup](https://rustup.rs/). The repository pins the toolchain version in `rust/rust-toolchain.toml`, and rustup installs that version automatically during the build:
+
+```bash
+curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
+source "$HOME/.cargo/env"
+```
+
+<Accordion title="Install without Rust">
+
+To skip the Rust extensions, set `SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none` when you install:
+
+```bash
+SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none pip install -e "python"
+```
+
+Basic model serving works without them. Features backed by a Rust extension, such as the gRPC server, build their extension with Cargo the first time you use them, so they still need the Rust toolchain at that point.
+
+</Accordion>
 
 **Get the source**
 
@@ -302,6 +326,18 @@ export CUDA_HOME="/path/to/cuda"
 
 For a versioned installation, this is typically `/usr/local/cuda-VERSION`. Alternatively, install FlashInfer first using the [FlashInfer installation instructions](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/installation.html), then retry the SGLang installation.
 
+### nvcc not found
+
+If the server exits during startup with `Failed to build JIT module` and `nvcc: not found`, or with `Could not find nvcc`, SGLang cannot find the CUDA Toolkit. Install CUDA Toolkit 13, or set `CUDA_HOME` to an existing installation as described in [CUDA_HOME](#cuda_home).
+
+### Triton falls back to CPU
+
+On an NVIDIA GPU, the warning `Triton is not supported on current platform, roll back to CPU.` usually means Triton could not compile its launcher, not that the GPU is unsupported. The server then fails with `Failed to find C compiler` or `Python.h: No such file or directory`. Install a C compiler and the Python development headers, as described in the pip / uv tab.
+
+### cargo is required
+
+If installing from source fails with `cargo is required to discover the Rust extension modules`, install the Rust toolchain, or set `SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none` to install without the Rust extensions. See the From source tab.
+
 ### FlashInfer
 
 - [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer) is the default attention kernel backend. It only supports sm75 and above. If you encounter any FlashInfer-related issues on sm75+ devices (e.g., T4, A10, A100, L4, L40S, H100), please switch to other kernels by adding `--attention-backend triton --sampling-backend pytorch` and open an issue on GitHub.
